column1: # CsvLoader adversarial byte fixtures -- geography.data.CsvLoader, JDK 17.0.19
# Produced by websim/pipeline/java-exporter/src-csv (WP5). Every outcome below is
# what the CERTIFIED loader did with these exact bytes, not what the spec says.
# CASE\tname\tmode\tinput_hex   then ROWS\tn | THROW\tmessage_hex, ROW lines, END.
# Hex is of UTF-8 bytes; an empty string is an empty token.
# why plain-crlf: CRLF is one terminator, not two
# why plain-cr: bare CR is a readLine terminator too
# why no-final-terminator: a final unterminated line is still a line
# why trailing-terminator: a trailing terminator produces NO extra empty line
# why bom-header: leading U+FEFF is stripped from the header
# why bom-midfile: a BOM on a DATA line is data: it is not stripped, and U+FEFF > U+0020 so trim keeps it
# why bom-only-line: a line holding only U+FEFF is NOT blank to Java trim() -- JS String.trim() would skip it
# why quoted-comma: quoted comma is not a separator
# why escaped-quote: "" is one literal quote
# why quote-opens-midfield: a quote may open mid-field; the state machine has no 'quoted fields start at the field' rule
# why unterminated-quote: an unterminated quote emits the text accumulated so far -- no throw
# why empty-quotes: "" is the empty field
# why trim-quoted: EVERY field is trimmed, quoted content included
# why trim-unquoted: unquoted fields trimmed too
# why trim-nbsp: Java trim() strips <= U+0020 ONLY: U+00A0 survives, JS String.prototype.trim() would eat it
# why trim-control: trim() strips ANY code unit <= U+0020, including U+0001 and U+001F
# why trim-nul: NUL is <= U+0020 and is trimmed like whitespace
# why short-row: short rows are padded with ""
# why extra-fields: fields beyond the header are silently dropped
# why trailing-comma: a trailing comma produces a final empty field
# why single-field: no comma at all
# why dup-headers: read: LinkedHashMap keeps the FIRST position and the LAST value; readStrict throws
# why dup-headers-blank: two empty header names are duplicates too
# why empty-file: read returns []; readStrict throws 'file is empty'
# why header-only: zero rows, no error
# why strict-field-count: readStrict rejects a wrong field count
# why strict-lineno-after-blank: lineNo increments BEFORE the blank-line skip, so the blank still advances it
# why header-quoted: quoted header names are trimmed too
# why crlf-inside-quotes-impossible: there are NO multi-line quoted fields: the reader works line by line, so this is two lines
